correctness.rationale: The finite domain and ordered/base-five encoding are explicit. Universal pair mergeability is equivalent to synchronizability by repeatedly merging two current image states. For each unordered pair of states, shortest merging length equals the first synchronous fixed-point stage of its two successors, with singleton successors terminal; all ten pairs being reached is exactly synchronizing. An independently written and compiled C++17 enumerator scanned all 5^10=9,765,625 encodings, not a sample, reproduced the synchronizing count and all five histogram bins, and independently enumerated all 9,120 maximizers. Its 240 state-permutation/letter-swap transformations per maximizer yield 38 nonoverlapping classes each of size 240, 9,120/9,120 strong connectivity, and exact rank-pair distribution 8/12/18. Source census.cpp and check_independent.cpp were read and their recurrences compared to the independently implemented synchronous method. These finite exhaustive counts make only a five-state result, not an n-state theorem.
